Eight boot phases and two deferred task identities. Adapter retirement has one outgoing/replacement pair, shared or distinct adapters, one active write or none, and two stop callbacks. Restore replacement has three runtime identities, four build calls, one initially admitted owner and authority closure only between requests. Shared-query handoff has four initialization modes, three handles for one physical connection, one unrelated handle, two queries, at most two handoffs, and one final close. Shared callback retirement has one outgoing admitted write, one or two published replacements, and strict or fast final stop.

Twelve hot-reload cases cover shared/distinct PGlite, actual HTTP/SQLite retention callbacks, and detached queries outside the outgoing runtime dirty snapshot. Four of these test live, identical, chained and unrelated scheduler handles. Three use authenticated HTTP with held PGlite retention writes, including failed completion and durable readback. Four additional restored-host cases cover actual startEliza evaluator retention past the fast cap, stop/start, closed and invalid authority, and durable persona/database readback.

ReplySettles assumes weak fairness of reply once a request exists. ReplyWithoutFairness intentionally has a stuttering counterexample. This does not prove HTTP scheduling, elapsed-time accuracy, disk-log retention or implementation refinement.
Two owner conversations, one selection/persistence attempt and one host replacement. Explicit missing or non-owner selection never falls back; a host change after the room read rejects persistence.
Four terminal prompt outcomes with or without prior reply delivery. HTTP/SQL tests cover cancelled, denied and failed turns, retained delivered replies and completed turns without chat text.

Room reads are atomic snapshots. Concurrent deletion after the read, in-flight database commits, real model/provider output, native packaging and unbounded concurrency remain outside this scope. No liveness claim.

HTTP scenario conformance checks ownership, stale snapshots, real stored task preservation and refusing removal during execution. Recovery returns an inactive task.
